title: Harnessing AI to Build Virtual Cells

parentSelection: Global tree-node selection by UCB; one parent program per expansion

mechanism.domainTask: Autonomous construction of gene perturbation-response prediction pipelines
mechanism.populationDetail: MCTS maintains a shared search tree of executable ML pipeline programs, with DAG-like reuse of successful ancestors and motifs in practice.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described; candidate programs and statistics remain in the MCTS tree, while structured memory stores feedback summaries.
mechanism.replacementDetail: New program nodes are inserted into the shared search tree and node statistics are updated; no tree pruning or survivor replacement policy is specified.
mechanism.generationDetail: The coding agent edits one selected parent program to alter pipeline architecture and/or training configuration; changes are iterative but are not restricted to a small code region.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Validation scores, runtime, cost, failures, successful motifs, and implementation details feed both MCTS statistics and coding-agent feedback memory.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The selected node/program is the direct parent for child expansion; DAG-like ancestry reuse is also supported.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Autonomous search spans whole trainable biological ML pipelines with pretrained encoders, distributed training, and persistent structured feedback memory.

provenance.sourcePdf: additional_papers/202604/Harnessing AI to Build Virtual Cells.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Distinguish Claude coding-agent model routing from multiple biological foundation encoders in generated artifacts; edit locality is not constrained to small changes.
